networks.label: Yeo 7-network cortical organisation
networks.method: Schaefer2018 parcels collapsed to their published Yeo network; carried per vertex, never interpolated
networks.composition: Cortical parcels: shares of assigned source vertices. NextBrain cortical regions: shares of assigned projected cortical voxels. Unassigned samples are excluded; these are not surface-area shares.

cab_np.label: Cole-Anticevic Brain-wide Network Partition (CAB-NP) v1.1.6
cab_np.license: CAB-NP License (Rutgers University and Yale University), non-commercial use only
cab_np.method: Each HCP-MMP1.0 area takes the network CAB-NP assigns it, matched by published area name in each hemisphere; carried per area, never per vertex

functional_regions.label: Functional divisions (Glasser 2016 sections; Glasser 2016, Rolls 2022 and Rolls 2023 named regions)
functional_regions.method: Each HCP-MMP1.0 area takes the section and, where a source names one, the named region whose published area list holds it, matched by area name in each hemisphere; carried per area, never per vertex

neuropsych_domains.label: Neuropsychological domains (Neurosynth consistency maps on HCP-MMP areas and aseg structures)
neuropsych_domains.license: Open Database License (ODbL) 1.0; derived area scores shared under the same licence
neuropsych_domains.method: Each domain's Neurosynth abstract term (version 7, TF-IDF at least 0.001); MKDA chi-square uniformity z with a 6 mm kernel on FSL's MNI152, read at each fsaverage vertex's MNI152 coordinate by registration fusion (RF-ANTs) and averaged per HCP-MMP area, and resampled onto SynthSeg's segmentation of the same MNI152 template and averaged per grey-matter structure. An area or structure belongs to every domain whose mean z reaches 3, its strength measured against the domain's cortical maximum; in the overview of the eleven assessment domains it takes the one whose z is the largest share of that domain's cortical maximum. Carried per area, never per vertex

receptor_fingerprints.label: Receptor fingerprints (Zilles and Palomero-Gallagher, EBRAINS)
receptor_fingerprints.method: Each EBRAINS receptor dataset's mean and SD over the sampled hemispheres, carried to the regions named after the area or structure it was measured in, in both hemispheres; never per vertex or voxel

stimulation_responses.label: Stimulation responses (Lyu et al. 2025)
stimulation_responses.method: Lyu et al. (2025)'s responding and non-responding stimulation–recording channel pairs, counted by the authors' anatomical labels and by side; a Destrieux parcel takes the label most cortical channels landing in it carry (fs_LR 32k → fsaverage sphere), and deep structures take labels by name

functional_connectivity.label: Functional connectivity (resting fMRI, HCP young adults, Domhof et al. 2021)
functional_connectivity.method: The Fisher-z mean of 200 HCP young adults' resting-state Pearson correlations between the parcel-mean BOLD series of Julich-Brain 3.1 areas in MNI152 space; each area takes the parcel of the same name

disorder_effects.label: Brain differences in disorders (ENIGMA consortium)
disorder_effects.method: Each ENIGMA working group's case–control Cohen's d (patients minus controls, adjusted for intracranial volume) per Desikan-Killiany region's cortical thickness and per subcortical volume, as the ENIGMA Toolbox republishes it; a region carries a difference only where its table's false discovery rate stays below 0.05

boundary_certainty.method: For each pair of touching NextBrain labels in one hemisphere, the voxels of either label with a face neighbour in the other, on the segmentation grid; of those, the ones where NextBrain's two most probable labels were this pair and the winner's posterior led by less than the margin

segmentation_agreement.method: Each NextBrain learning-unit union validation compares with aseg, voxelised onto aseg's 1 mm grid: a voxel belongs to the union when more than half of the 0.4 mm voxels whose nearest aseg voxel it is belong to it. Voxels are then counted where both segmentations, only aseg or only NextBrain label the structure

cerebellar_functions.label: Functional cerebellar regions (Nettekoven et al. 2024)

regions.name: M1 · oculomotor
regions.description: The oculomotor vermis, most active for saccades, and also during reading, film watching and visual search.
regions.description_fr: Le vermis oculomoteur, le plus actif lors des saccades, et aussi pendant la lecture, un film ou la recherche visuelle.

regions.name: M2 · tongue
regions.description: A lateral part most active for tongue movements and a vermal part active for several body movements.
regions.description_fr: Une partie latérale la plus active lors des mouvements de la langue et une partie vermienne active pour plusieurs mouvements du corps.

regions.name: M3 · hand
regions.description: Selectively active for movements of the hand on its own side.
regions.description_fr: Sélectivement active lors des mouvements de la main du même côté.

regions.name: M4 · lower body
regions.description: Most active for movements of the lower body, such as foot flexion and contraction of the gluteal muscles.
regions.description_fr: La plus active lors des mouvements du bas du corps, comme la flexion du pied et la contraction des fessiers.

regions.name: A1 · action
regions.description: Active when actions are observed, and especially for tasks that require spatial simulation, such as mental rotation.
regions.description_fr: Active lors de l’observation d’actions, et surtout pour les tâches de simulation spatiale, comme la rotation mentale.

regions.name: A2 · action
regions.description: A classic action-observation region, with little response to tasks that neither show nor perform an action.
regions.description_fr: Une région classique d’observation de l’action, peu active pour les tâches qui ne montrent ni n’exécutent d’action.

regions.name: A3 · action
regions.description: Active when actions are observed and also when movements are imagined.
regions.description_fr: Active lors de l’observation d’actions et aussi lors de mouvements imaginés.

regions.name: D1 · multiple demand
regions.description: Active for executive control, such as updating, shifting and inhibition; the most medial part of Crus I and II.
regions.description_fr: Active lors du contrôle exécutif, comme la mise à jour, l’alternance et l’inhibition ; la partie la plus médiane des Crus I et II.

regions.name: D2 · multiple demand
regions.description: Active for executive control; the innermost layer of the demand regions, repeated in lobule IX.
regions.description_fr: Active lors du contrôle exécutif ; la couche la plus interne des régions de demande, répétée dans le lobule IX.

regions.name: D3 · multiple demand
regions.description: Active for executive control; the outermost layer of the demand regions, with vermal parts in lobules IV and IX.
regions.description_fr: Active lors du contrôle exécutif ; la couche la plus externe des régions de demande, avec des parties vermiennes dans les lobules IV et IX.

regions.name: D4 · multiple demand
regions.description: The smallest region, functionally closest to D1; the most lateral of the demand regions.
regions.description_fr: La plus petite région, fonctionnellement la plus proche de D1 ; la plus latérale des régions de demande.

regions.name: S1 · social, linguistic, spatial
regions.description: The most medial of these regions, in the depth of the horizontal fissure; on the right, most active for language, such as verb generation.
regions.description_fr: La plus médiane de ces régions, au fond de la fissure horizontale ; à droite, la plus active pour le langage, comme la génération de verbes.

regions.name: S2 · social, linguistic, spatial
regions.description: Most active for social processing, such as a theory-of-mind task on the right and an animated film on the left; active at rest.
regions.description_fr: La plus active pour le traitement social, comme une tâche de théorie de l’esprit à droite et un film d’animation à gauche ; active au repos.

regions.name: S3 · social, linguistic, spatial
regions.description: Overlaps S2 and S4 so much that it can be told apart from them only in an individual's own data; active at rest.
regions.description_fr: Recouvre tant S2 et S4 qu’on ne l’en distingue que dans les données propres d’un individu ; active au repos.

regions.name: S4 · social, linguistic, spatial
regions.description: The most lateral tips of Crus I and II; most active for imagination and self-projection, such as imagining walking through a familiar home.
regions.description_fr: Les extrémités les plus latérales des Crus I et II ; la plus active pour l’imagination et la projection de soi, comme se promener en pensée dans un lieu familier.

regions.name: S5 · social, linguistic, spatial
regions.description: Active for imagination, spatial working memory and action observation, between this domain and the action regions.
regions.description_fr: Active pour l’imagination, la mémoire de travail spatiale et l’observation d’actions, entre ce domaine et les régions d’action.

cerebellar_functions.method: The SUIT cerebellar template registered to this brain's skull-stripped T1, kept to its infratentorial compartment, with SynthMorph (joint affine and deformable); the atlas carried across by nearest neighbour and kept to this brain's cerebellar cortex. Each lobule's shares count its own voxels

striatal_networks.label: Striatal networks (Choi et al. 2012)
striatal_networks.method: FSL's MNI152 template (MNI152NLin6Asym), skull-stripped, registered to this brain's skull-stripped T1 with SynthMorph (joint affine and deformable); the atlas's loose mask carried across by nearest neighbour and kept to this brain's caudate, putamen and accumbens. A voxel the atlas does not reach takes the network of the nearest voxel it reaches in the same structure. Each region's shares count its own voxels. A structure under 100 mm³ takes no shares, and names none round it: no landing error was measured for maps registered onto this brain

coordinate_spaces.label: Published coordinates

spaces.label: MNI152NLin2009cAsym
spaces.description: ICBM 152 nonlinear asymmetric 2009c, fMRIPrep's default output space
spaces.citation: Fonov VS, Evans AC, McKinstry RC, Almli CR, Collins DL (2009) Unbiased nonlinear average age-appropriate brain templates from birth to adulthood. NeuroImage 47:S102
spaces.license: MNI template licence (use, copy, modify and distribute with the copyright notice)
spaces.copyright: Copyright (C) 1993–2004 Louis Collins, McConnell Brain Imaging Centre, Montreal Neurological Institute, McGill University.

coordinate_spaces.method: This brain is MNI152NLin2009cAsym itself, reconstructed with its header scaled by 0.9: a coordinate's millimetres times 0.9, in FreeSurfer's surface RAS. Nothing is registered.

cortical_layers.label: Cortical layers (BigBrain, one histological brain)
cortical_layers.method: Each cortical parcel's area-weighted mean thickness of each of BigBrain's six layers (Wagstyl et al. 2020, resampled to fsaverage by BigBrainWarp) over the sum of the six, on the atlas's fsaverage annotation, carried to this brain's parcel of the same name; a parcel is published where BigBrain's layers cover at least 50% of its area. Cell densities are the EBRAINS patches' detected cells per layer over the layer's shrinkage-corrected volume, averaged over patches, carried to the Julich-Brain area of the same name in both hemispheres

display_geometry.method: Marching cubes, then bounded Taubin smoothing that moves no voxel centre across the surface
Marching cubes, then bounded Taubin smoothing that moves no voxel centre across the surface

detail_levels.label: Learning anatomy
detail_levels.palette_method: Distinct teaching colours for display units, not the source LUT

display_geometry.method: Explicit source-label unions; bounded Taubin display smoothing

cerebellar_fissures.method: Lobule voxels below the midpoint of the lobules' and CSF's median T1, face-connected through such voxels to fluid outside the cerebellum

display_geometry.openness: _OPENNESS on CerebNet lobules: cosine-weighted share of rays from each vertex that clear the intact lobule surfaces together, a hit at d counting d / radius_mm open (appearance.occlusion)

boundary_convention: Barycentric vertex cells on mixed-label triangles
limitations: An averaged reference template: it is nobody's anatomy, and no part of it is clinically validated.
Destrieux labels are the template parcellation; no individual brain was measured to place them.
HCP-MMP is the published Mills fsaverage projection, resampled again onto this brain through FreeSurfer's registered spheres: two registrations, and native HCP space is neither of them.
Labels projected between brains are bounded by that registration, not by the accuracy of the published parcellation.
Destrieux labels identify gyri and sulci; HCP labels identify multimodal areas.
Subvertex label boundaries are visualization conventions, not measured boundaries.
FreeSurfer's subcortical segmentation uses a 1 mm grid; fine nuclei and cerebellar folia are unresolved in it.

NextBrain labels are this brain's own Bayesian segmentation at 0.4 mm, estimated from a 1 mm T1 with a histological atlas as prior: where neighbouring structures share their T1 contrast, the atlas rather than the scan places the boundary between them.
Learning anatomy is a derived overview of explicit label unions, with display smoothing bounded to 0.6 mm. Measurements remain source-voxel counts; smoothness does not add anatomical resolution.
Learning brainstem territories omit separately displayed nuclei and pathways; they are not complete brainstem subdivisions.
Learning publishes the cerebellar cortex and the deep nuclei, but not cerebellar white matter, which would enclose the nuclei; the nuclei therefore sit in the space it occupies.
Learning cerebellar lobules are FastSurfer CerebNet's segmentation of this brain's 1 mm T1 in SUIT nomenclature; vermis I–V is part of lobules I–IV and V, and folia are not resolved.

Averaging removes the folia and finer fissures of the cerebellar hemispheres from the template's T1, so the lobule borders there follow the white-matter branches and the shape CerebNet learned from individual brains, not fissures that can be seen.
Learning lobule surfaces leave out the lobule voxels the T1 reads as mostly fluid and open to the CSF, which shows the wider fissures; their volumes and placements are CerebNet's labels unchanged.
Cerebellar lobules are published as teaching surfaces only; MRI cuts carry no lobule labels.
Learning units come from three segmentations of the same brain (aseg, NextBrain and CerebNet), so surfaces from different sources can overlap slightly where they meet.
NextBrain nuclei below the geometry threshold, its white matter, its cerebellar cortical layers and its cortical parcels have no mesh and remain cut labels only.
Only one internal-anatomy detail level is drawn at a time; the coarse and fine layers segment the same anatomy.
Below NextBrain's lowest medullary voxel, the NextBrain level draws the teaching set's caudal medulla, which is FreeSurfer's brainstem label, so the medulla meets the spinal cord.
Internal solids are marching-cubes surfaces smoothed for display by at most 0.6 mm and never across a voxel centre; between voxel centres their boundaries are a display convention, not a measurement.
Where a segmented structure meets itself at a corner its surface pinches there and is not a two-manifold; validation counts those edges, and the volume each surface encloses stays definite.
NextBrain cortical parcels are published as ctx-rh- names for both hemispheres, an artefact of the reused label block; the hemisphere field is authoritative.

Boundary certainty is NextBrain's competition between its own labels: the share of a boundary where its two most probable labels were within 0.2 of each other. It is conditional on one registration and is not agreement with another segmentation; a confident boundary can still be misplaced.
Boundaries across the midline are not rated: each hemisphere is segmented separately and joined.

Segmentation agreement compares NextBrain, voxelised onto aseg's 1 mm grid, with aseg for five structures per side. Agreement between two segmentations of one scan is not accuracy, and neither is the reference; NextBrain's own boundary certainty does not measure it.
Cortical regions are surface patches; the solids that cap them at a cut are closed by extruding each patch to its corresponding white-surface vertices.

Each region's centroid is the mean of its voxel centres (a cortical parcel's, of its voxels in the cortical ribbon), and can lie outside a curved region; its anchor, where the linked MRI and a cut go to show it, is its own voxel nearest that centroid. A parcel no ribbon voxel carries is placed by its mid-ribbon surface points instead.
A cut assigns each source triangle to the parcel holding most of its vertices, so a parcel boundary on a cut can differ from the surface's barycentric boundary by one triangle.
Networks describe group resting-state functional connectivity from 1000 subjects, not a region's measured function in this brain.

Cortical parcel network shares count assigned source vertices; NextBrain cortical region shares count assigned projected cortical voxels. Unassigned samples are excluded. Neither is a surface-area fraction.
Networks are published in this template's space and are not resampled, but they remain a group average of other brains.
CAB-NP networks come from group resting-state connectivity of Human Connectome Project participants, not from this brain's measured function, and reach this brain through the same HCP-MMP projection.
CAB-NP assigns each HCP-MMP area whole to one network, so its colour boundaries are HCP-MMP's boundaries. It colours that atlas's areas only.
CAB-NP assigns the hemispheres separately; 13 areas belong to a different network on each side, as published.

Functional divisions are published groupings of HCP-MMP1.0 areas: the 22 sections of Glasser et al. (2016) and named regions from Glasser et al. (2016) and Rolls et al. (2022, 2023). They reach this brain through the HCP-MMP projection and are not measured in it.

A functional division's borders are HCP-MMP's area borders. No border is drawn for a name no source defines as a set of HCP-MMP areas: dorsomedial prefrontal cortex, a dorsolateral prefrontal cortex narrower than Glasser's section, the temporoparietal junction and the intraparietal sulcus have no named region and are shown only within Glasser's sections.

Glasser's supplement places six areas (23c, 52, PFcm, TF, a47r, pOFC) in one section in its Table 1 and in another in its section texts; the sections follow Table 1's primary column, and the alternative is published beside each.

Neuropsychological domains are Neurosynth consistency maps of the published activation literature, averaged over each HCP-MMP area on fsaverage and reaching this brain through its HCP-MMP projection. They show where studies using a domain's term report activation in groups of healthy people, not what this brain does, and not what damage to an area would impair.

Most terms are used by at least 100 studies. Eleven clinically pertinent ones rest on fewer, down to 74 (sustained attention, smell, navigation, verbal fluency, taste, interoception, gestures, object recognition, moral reasoning, arithmetic, speech perception); their maps are weaker evidence, and every function names its study count.
Consciousness (74 studies) was derived and left out: its map reached two areas, right MT at z 3.3 and the left fusiform face complex at 3.1, and no structure.

Each domain is one abstract term chosen to name the clinical domain, and a study counts when its abstract uses the term, whatever task it ran. Consistency z grows with the number of such studies, so domains backed by large literatures (attention, language, working memory) reach more areas than executive function or social cognition; regions engaged by most demanding tasks, such as the anterior insula and intraparietal sulcus, reach several domains.

Besides the cortex, each map is averaged over FreeSurfer's grey-matter structures (thalamus, caudate, putamen, pallidum, hippocampus, amygdala, accumbens, ventral diencephalon, cerebellar cortex and brainstem), each as a whole on SynthSeg's segmentation of the MNI152 template the maps are computed on. The 6 mm kernel is large beside the smaller nuclei, and studies report fewer subcortical coordinates, so these are weaker evidence than the cortical areas. White matter and NextBrain's finer nuclei are not scored, and a lesion check on them is reported as not measured. The teaching set's caudate, putamen, both pallidal segments, accumbens, thalamus, hippocampus and amygdala are drawn with the score of the structure most of each lies in on this brain; its other units, the geniculate bodies among them, which FreeSurfer files under the ventral diencephalon, are not scored.

Neurosynth's MNI152 maps reach fsaverage by registration fusion (Wu et al. 2018), each vertex read where 1,490 people's registrations place it in MNI152 on average, at mid-thickness. That mapping places group results, not any one person's folds, and areas narrower than the 6 mm kernel share their neighbours' values.

Receptor fingerprints are densities measured by in vitro autoradiography in two to six post-mortem brains (Zilles and Palomero-Gallagher, via EBRAINS), pooled over the hemispheres sampled. They reach this brain only by the name of the area or structure measured and are not measured in it; both hemispheres show the same values.

Only the Julich-Brain areas and the deep structures a dataset names carry a fingerprint. Areas 9, 46 and 47 are published but name no Julich-Brain area and are left out. A structure the dataset names as a whole, such as the globus pallidus or the anterior thalamic nucleus, gives the same values to each of its subdivisions.
A published value known to be wrong is withheld and the reason is published with it: Area ifs1's D1 SD equals the same file's A1 mean.

Stimulation responses are counts of stereo-EEG channel pairs from 27 people with focal epilepsy (Lyu et al. 2025), pooled by the authors' anatomical labels and by side. They are not measured in this brain, both hemispheres show the same values, and a person with many channels weighs more than one with few.

A Destrieux parcel takes an author label only when at least 10 cortical channels from 3 people land in it through fs_LR 32k → fsaverage surface registration and 60% of them carry that label; other parcels, and the HCP-MMP, Julich-Brain and Schaefer atlases, take none (Julich-Brain areas show F-TRACT's rates instead). Deep structures take labels by name, and the thalamus takes the authors' three positional sites, not nuclei.

Functional connectivity is the group mean of 200 healthy young adults (HCP, ages 22–35) at rest, measured in MNI152 space on Julich-Brain's volumetric map, not in this brain: an area takes the parcel of its name. A correlation is not a connection, and without global signal regression nearly every pair correlates positively.

Disorder effects are group differences between thousands of patients and controls scanned elsewhere, reported per Desikan-Killiany region and FreeSurfer structure, not measured in this brain. Most are small (|d| below 0.2 is common): patients and controls overlap almost entirely, so no difference says anything about one person. Medication, illness duration and site differ between the cohorts and are only partly adjusted for.

Functional cerebellar regions are a group atlas (Nettekoven et al. 2024) fused from seven task-based fMRI datasets and registered onto this brain from the SUIT template; this brain's function was not measured. Individual functional boundaries differ from the group's, and the authors show that an individual's own localizer data place them better.

Registration from a group template places lobule borders a few millimetres off: SUIT's own lobules, carried by the same warp, meet this brain's CerebNet lobules at a mean Dice of 0.76. A region's border on a cut is approximate; a lobule's shares, summed over its whole volume, are steadier.

Striatal networks are a group atlas (Choi et al. 2012) from 1,000 adults' resting-state connectivity, registered onto this brain from FSL's MNI152 template; this brain's function was not measured. Each voxel takes only the cortical network its connectivity most resembles.

Registration from a group template places network borders a few millimetres off. The atlas reached at least 89% of each striatal structure on this brain (least: right accumbens); the rest takes the network of the nearest voxel it reached in the same structure.

Choi et al. give each voxel a confidence: the fraction of its 25 most correlated cortical vertices that belong to its network. Of this brain's labelled striatum, 1% falls below 0.5, where its network holds only a plurality, and 5% was filled rather than reached; the cut draws both paler.
Choi et al. are least confident around the dorsal putamen, where signal from the adjacent insula is only partly removed, so a putamen's salience share may partly reflect the insula.

This brain is the MNI152NLin2009cAsym template at 0.9 of its size, so a coordinate in that space is placed by scaling alone, with no registration. Coordinates and maps in any other template are not placed on it.
Cortical coordinates are reported as the regions within 5 mm, as on an individual brain.
An MNI coordinate whose template is not stated is read as MNI152NLin2009cAsym.

Cortical layers are one brain's: BigBrain, a man of 65 examined post mortem. Its six layers were segmented by a neural network at 83% per-point accuracy (Wagstyl et al. 2020) and carried to fsaverage by registration (BigBrainWarp); each parcel here shows that brain's layers at the matching place, by parcel name, not layers measured in this brain. Shares, not millimetres, are shown, since a share is unaffected by the tissue's overall shrinkage.
Cortex that has no six layers, the hippocampus and the olfactory (piriform) cortex, is left out, as is a parcel BigBrain's layers cover on less than 50% of its area.

Cell densities count every cell body a network detected in 5 to 11 patches per area of the same brain, not neurons alone, and reach a region only by the name of the Julich-Brain area the patches were cut from; both hemispheres show the same values.
BigBrain and the cell datasets are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: non-commercial use only, and derived work is shared alike.

F-TRACT stimulation responses are rates of stereo-EEG stimulation–recording pairs from 613 people with focal epilepsy, aggregated by F-TRACT over Julich-Brain 3.0 areas in MNI152 space. They are not measured in this brain; each hemisphere shows its own values. A rate is published from 10 pairs and drawn here only from 3 implantations.

A Julich-Brain area takes the F-TRACT area of the same name, not of the same place: F-TRACT placed contacts with Julich-Brain's volumetric map in MNI152, while this surface carries the published fsaverage map. Areas Julich-Brain 3.1 added from 3.0's gap maps, and its subicular complex, take none.

F-TRACT peak delays come from people with focal epilepsy. Each is a median across the responding stimulation–recording pairs of every implantation that tested the pair, not one person's delay, published from 10 responses within 50 ms and shown only where the rate is drawn. A response may arrive through more than one synapse, and the peak includes the time the recorded area takes to respond, so a delay is not a conduction time along one fibre. Distances are between the two areas' centroids in this brain, not between the contacts. Onset delay is not shown: the data descriptor defines it two ways.

scripts/segment_nextbrain.py: SuperSynth, then NextBrain Bayesian segmentation (segment_fireants.py --mode invivo --device cpu) of each hemisphere at 0.4 mm, joined on one 0.4 mm surface-RAS grid

crop.rule: bounding box of brain.mgz > 0, plus 20 voxels, within the grid

hemisphere_join.method: nearest neighbour from each hemisphere's own grid onto one surface-RAS grid
hemisphere_join.overlap_rule: sign of SuperSynth's MNI x coordinate at the voxel centre, the rule FreeSurfer splits hemispheres by

near_ties.rule: the runner-up label wherever NextBrain's winning posterior led it by less than the margin; 0 elsewhere and where the runner-up is background
near_ties.posteriors: written by scripts/freesurfer/run_patched.py from segment_fireants.py's label loop, beside a label update it leaves unchanged

runtime_workarounds.conv3d_slices: FreeSurfer 8.2's arm64 torch 2.1.2 has no oneDNN, so CPU conv3d builds a whole-volume im2col buffer (about 90 GB for SuperSynth). scripts/freesurfer/conv3d_slices.py computes the same stride-1 convolution as a sum over kernel depth of 2D convolutions of shifted slices: the same products in a different summation order, matching torch conv3d to 1e-5 relative. Only a convolution whose im2col buffer would reach 1 GiB is sliced; smaller ones run in torch itself, so NextBrain's bias field fit keeps the exact zeros it takes logs of. FireANTs keeps the builtin F.conv3d, which its TorchScript functions bind when they compile.
runtime_workarounds.supersynth_memory_releases: SuperSynth's inference.py drops its first-pass network outputs before the flipped pass, and the flipped outputs once they are averaged in. Only when memory is freed changes.
runtime_workarounds.opencv_stand_in: FreeSurfer 8.2's macOS Python has no OpenCV, yet ERC_bayesian_segmentation's ext/my_functions.py imports cv2 at module level for one helper that asserts False on entry. A stand-in module lets the import succeed and raises if any attribute of it is used.

stimulation_ftract.label: Stimulation responses (F-TRACT v2307)
stimulation_ftract.method: F-TRACT's probability that stimulating one Julich-Brain 3.0 area evoked a response in another, with its stimulation–recording pairs and implantations, and the median delay to the response's first peak, from 613 people; each Julich-Brain area takes the F-TRACT area of the same name, and a delay is set against the distance between the two areas' centroids in this brain
